plan_a_advantages: More targeted training for speed (threshold sessions)
plan_b_advantages: Includes a hill workout, beneficial for trail running strength
Longer runs provide a good base of aerobic fitness
reasoning: For a trail runner aiming to become faster, Plan A is the superior choice. It strategically incorporates two threshold sessions, crucial for building the sustained power needed for faster paces on trails. Plan B, while including a hill workout, relies more heavily on longer, moderate-intensity runs, which are less effective for directly improving speed. Plan A’s focus on threshold work, combined with consistent easy runs, provides a more targeted approach to enhancing the athlete’s running economy and power, which are key determinants of trail speed. Furthermore, the shorter duration of the hard sessions in Plan A minimizes the risk of overtraining, allowing for better recovery and adaptation.
